Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap. A few clarifying items from our side:

- For the deletion SLAs we need:
  * Deletion of user-provided PII (e.g., name, email) after an admin request within a maximum SLA - are you able to commit to an RTO/RPO-style number (e.g., 30 days / 7 days)?
  * Deletion of generated content (model outputs) - is this tied to user data deletion or separate?
  * Backups: how long do backups store deleted data? Is there a separate retention window?

- For logs: we store request metadata for troubleshooting and billing; we need to know where these are retained and if they contain any user-submitted content or PII.

We'll attach our vendor security questionnaire in a follow-up email from security@amayahealth.com - please look out for it. Procurement is targeting a Jan 15th kickoff for pilot but we're flexible if security review extends.

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Data retention / deletion SLAs and log retention (Amaya)

Marissa / Neha,

Quick draft answers we can provide back to Amaya Security. I'll clean these up and populate the spreadsheet, but flagging the key points here:

1) SOC 2: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II audit in Q2 2026. Attached summary: SOC2-Type2-Report-2026.pdf. Our control scope covers the Hosted API and our control plane; Dedicated instances are covered under customer-specific attachments - we can provide a coverage statement for Dedicated/Private on request.

2) Data retention / deletion SLAs:
  - Customer-managed user data (profile, PII) deletion: We perform logical deletion within 48 hours and physical deletion from primary stores within 30 days; final removal from backups can take up to 90 days depending on backup rotation cadence.
  - Generated content (model outputs): By default we retain for 30 days for quality/compliance monitoring; customers can request a 0-day retention policy on a per-contract basis (and we'll provide an option in Dedicated/Private).
  - Audit logs / request traces: Application-level logs (non-content metadata) retained for 365 days; request traces that may include content are redacted by default and retained for 90 days.

3) Backups: Backups are encrypted, and the rotation policy is weekly full + daily incrementals; deleted data can persist in backups until they roll off (up to 90 days). For customers requiring shorter backup retention, we can discuss a dedicated backup retention SLA on Dedicated/Private deployments.

4) Encryption & key management: Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256; keys are managed via our KMS. We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Dedicated/Private and have HSM integrations for enterprise tiers.

5) Subprocessors: We maintain a subprocessors list (can provide a current PDF).

Attachments I will include in the intake spreadsheet: retention-matrix.xlsx (with the SLA rows above) and backup-policy-summary.pdf.

If this looks good I'll complete the spreadsheet and return to security@amayahealth.com by EOD.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Staff Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
